materials.title: Why the Pen Stopped Writing
materials.text:
At a writing workshop, a pen stopped halfway through a line. The barrel still contained ____1____, the coloured liquid used to make marks, so the problem was not simply an empty pen. The tutor opened a model to show how the liquid reached the page.

The supply was held in a ____2____, a storage space inside the pen. In this design, it took the form of a replaceable ____3____ that could be removed when empty. Other pens used different filling arrangements, so the class kept the general storage role separate from this particular container.

The metal writing tip was the ____4____. Beneath it, a grooved ____5____ guided liquid towards the tip and helped regulate movement. Narrow spaces allowed ____6____ action to assist liquid movement through the system. This was different from a pump forcing a measured dose out with each stroke.

As liquid left, ____7____ needed to enter the storage space. Otherwise the balance of ____8____ could oppose continued movement. The transparent demonstration model made both routes easier to discuss without implying that every ordinary pen had a clear barrel.

The liquid's ____9____ concerned its resistance to flowing. A mixture that moved differently from the intended ink could behave poorly in the same passages. In the pen being examined, the exposed tip had become ____10____ after being left uncapped. Moistening and cleaning were handled by the tutor under the workshop's instructions.

The exercise replaced the simple question whether ink remained with a description of connected routes and material conditions. A full storage space was necessary for writing, but it was not sufficient if the path to the page had been interrupted.

materials.title: The Mushroom Was Not the Whole Fungus
materials.text:
A woodland display showed a mushroom emerging from a fallen log. A visitor called it a small plant growing from the tree. The guide explained that the mushroom was a ____1____ body of a fungus, a structure involved in reproduction rather than the whole organism.

Its rounded upper part was the ____2____. Thin plates beneath it were ____3____ in this example. Reproductive particles called ____4____ developed on specialised structures there. They were not seeds containing a plant embryo. The guide used a labelled illustration because mushroom forms differ, and the description did not apply to every species.

The upright supporting part was the ____5____. Inside the log, fine fungal threads formed ____6____, the collective vegetative material of the fungus. Together they made an extensive ____7____ that was largely hidden from a person looking only at the mushroom.

The dead wood served as a ____8____, the material on which this fungus grew. The fungus helped ____9____ it, breaking complex material down through its biological activity. The example was about a decomposer; the guide did not infer that every fungus had the same relation to a living host.

Available ____10____ affected the growth conditions, so the guide noted that the log was damp. A mushroom appearing after rain did not mean the entire fungus had suddenly come into existence overnight.

The display concluded with a clear boundary: recognising these structural roles was not a method for deciding whether a wild mushroom was edible. Similar-looking forms could have very different properties. The educational point was to distinguish the conspicuous reproductive structure from the less visible organism and its relationship with the surrounding material.

materials.title: Warmth in the Spaces
materials.text:
A clothing display compared fabric samples around containers of warm water. The containers supplied ____1____, energy transferred because of a temperature difference. The garments were not creating an unlimited supply of warmth by themselves.

The arrangement of clothing in several ____2____ allowed air spaces between materials. Air held relatively still in those spaces was ____3____ rather than circulating freely. The display described reduced transfer as ____4____, resistance to heat passing through the arrangement.

One route of transfer was ____5____, passage through materials by contact without bulk movement of the material. Another was ____6____, involving movement of a fluid such as air. Energy could also pass as ____7____, electromagnetic transfer that did not require the same contact route. The tutor named all three without pretending that only one occurred in ordinary clothing.

Water changed the conditions. ____8____ in a garment meant that liquid was present where a dry comparison had contained air. The cooling associated with ____9____ occurred when liquid became vapour. The display did not infer warmth from fabric appearance alone.

A fluffy sample lost some of its air spaces when it was ____10____, pressed into a smaller volume. Simply carrying more material did not guarantee the original arrangement would remain effective. Fit, wetness and movement also mattered.

The class used the comparison to ask what a layer actually did under stated conditions. It did not rank every fabric for every climate or activity. A label describing one property, such as resistance to water, could not by itself supply a complete account of comfort and heat transfer.

questions.explanation: L heat：temperature-difference energy transfer为热；thickness尺寸不是能量。

questions.prompt: Warmth in the Spaces: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.

questions.explanation: D insulation：resistance to heat transfer为隔热；radiation等为传热机制而非总体阻碍。

questions.prompt: Warmth in the Spaces: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: G convection：movement of fluid为对流；conduction通过接触，radiation电磁机制。

questions.prompt: Warmth in the Spaces: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: N radiation：electromagnetic transfer为辐射；evaporation水相变不是全部电磁传递。

questions.prompt: Warmth in the Spaces: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.

materials.title: The Wheel Was Not Bent
materials.text:
A photography class compared images of a rotating wheel. One image showed soft edges along the direction of movement. Another showed relatively clear spokes that seemed oddly slanted. The tutor warned that these appearances need not have the same cause.

The light-sensitive surface in the camera was the ____1____. An ____2____ was the period during which light contributed to an image. Its ____3____ described how long that period lasted. If the wheel moved substantially within that interval, motion ____4____ could appear, spreading a feature across several positions.

In one camera design, the image area was exposed in successive ____5____ rather than all at one instant. This was called a ____6____ shutter arrangement. Different parts of a moving object could therefore be recorded at slightly different times.

The resulting change of shape was a form of ____7____. A spoke that looked bent in the image did not prove that the physical wheel had bent. The pattern depended on the object's motion and the timing across the recording surface.

A ____8____ shutter arrangement treated the relevant image area over the same exposure interval in the simplified comparison. It could reduce that timing difference, although motion during the interval could still soften edges. The tutor therefore kept simultaneous recording separate from an infinitely short exposure.

The wheel's ____9____ supplied the changing positions in the example. A ____10____ object would not show that particular motion-dependent effect under the same setup. The lesson joined observation with camera operation instead of using every unusual shape as direct evidence about the photographed object. It also distinguished a sharp-looking edge from a guarantee that all parts of the image represented the same moment.

questions.explanation: E sensor：light-sensitive camera surface为传感器；lens透镜汇光不是感光面。

questions.explanation: A exposure：light contributes期间为曝光；aperture光圈开口非时间事件。

questions.explanation: B rolling：rolling shutter逐行快门；global全局相反条件下段。

questions.prompt: The Wheel Was Not Bent: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: H distortion：shape change为畸变；blur软边不是同一现象，本例可相对清晰而斜。

questions.prompt: The Wheel Was Not Bent: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.

materials.title: Ten Nearby Measurements
materials.text:
A field team measured soil properties at many points. Its first analysis treated observations as ____1____, assuming that knowing one measurement provided no information about another after the model's stated conditions were considered. A map made that assumption questionable: nearby measurements often moved together.

The relation was ____2____ because it concerned location in space. Association of the same variable across locations was ____3____. The team did not infer from that name alone that every nearby pair had identical values or that the pattern necessarily arose from a single cause.

Separation was measured as ____4____ under a specified geometry. The scale beyond which the model treated remaining association as negligible was its ____5____ in the simplified example. The meaning of that parameter depended on the chosen model, rather than being a universal feature read directly from any map.

Dense groups of nearby sample points formed ____6____. Adding many points within the same group could reveal local variation without supplying as much independent information about the whole area as the raw count suggested. The ____7____ sample size expressed that distinction under stated assumptions; it was not obtained merely by renaming the number of rows.

Sampling ____8____ concerned repeated observations at suitable units. Closely related points were not automatically equivalent to repeating the entire study in new independent areas. The design therefore recorded how locations had been selected.

The investigators estimated ____9____, the variation in the measured values, while examining how spatial dependence affected uncertainty. A narrow reported interval suggested high ____10____ only relative to the model that produced it. Ignoring dependence could make an interval look more informative than justified.

The lesson linked sampling geometry to inference. More measurements could be useful, but their contribution depended on where they were taken and on the question. Neither a large table nor a colourful map could remove the need to explain relationships among observations.

questions.explanation: A independent：conditional no information relation为独立；random随机选点不自动保证测值独立。

questions.prompt: Ten Nearby Measurements: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: D spatial：locations in space为空间的；biased有偏指估计系统偏差，不命名空间关联属性。

questions.prompt: Ten Nearby Measurements: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: G autocorrelation：same variable cross locations关联为空间自相关；replication重复样本不命名变量与自身异地关联。

questions.prompt: Ten Nearby Measurements: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: B distance：separation under geometry为距离；resolution分辨尺度不是任意两点间分离量。

questions.prompt: Ten Nearby Measurements: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: E range：model scale correlation negligible为相关范围；boundary研究边界非相关衰减尺度。

questions.prompt: Ten Nearby Measurements: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: C clusters：dense groups points为簇；neighbours是邻居点，不直接以groups说明组群实体。

questions.prompt: Ten Nearby Measurements: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: J effective：effective sample size按相关调整信息量；random sample size非此术语，raw count已对照。

questions.prompt: Ten Nearby Measurements: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: I replication：sampling replication为重复，适当单位重测；resolution空间精细度不等重复观察。

questions.prompt: Ten Nearby Measurements: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: M variance：variation statistic为方差；precision估计不确定性精细程度与数值间变异量不同。

questions.prompt: Ten Nearby Measurements: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: F precision：narrow interval表估计精密度；variance可影响区间但本句high variance与窄区间推向相反。

materials.title: A Fixed Payment, a Changing Value
materials.text:
A finance class examined a simplified fixed-rate bond held to a stated date. The borrowed amount to be repaid was the ____1____. Scheduled interest payments were described by the ____2____ terms. A promise of fixed payments did not guarantee that the borrower would always fulfil it.

The date for final repayment was ____3____. This was distinct from ____4____, a measure used to summarise the sensitivity of the bond's value to changes in interest rates under specified assumptions. Two instruments ending on the same date could distribute payments differently and need not have the same sensitivity.

In the secondary market, the bond had a ____5____, the amount at which it could be exchanged under current conditions. Its quoted ____6____ related the payment stream to that amount through a stated calculation. The coupon rate alone did not determine the return available to someone buying at a different market value.

Returns expressed without an inflation adjustment were ____7____. Returns adjusted for changes in purchasing power were ____8____. A positive result under the first description did not ensure that the holder could buy more goods at the end.

Failure to make a promised payment was ____9____ under the terms of the example. Separately, ____10____ concerned how readily the bond could be sold without an adverse price effect. An asset could be hard to sell even when no scheduled payment had yet been missed.

The exercise separated contractual promises, market valuation and realised outcomes. It did not recommend a purchase or claim that one measure captured every investment risk. Students learned why a familiar percentage needed a definition before comparison: a coupon, a market-implied measure and an inflation-adjusted result answered different questions.

questions.explanation: F principal：borrowed amount repaid为本金；coupon利息条款、collateral担保物不是借款本金。

questions.prompt: A Fixed Payment, a Changing Value: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: A coupon：scheduled interest为票息条款；dividend股息属于股权分配，不能换债息。

questions.prompt: A Fixed Payment, a Changing Value: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: N maturity：final repayment date为到期；duration反映现金流及价格敏感性，非到期日。

questions.prompt: A Fixed Payment, a Changing Value: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: J duration：interest-rate price sensitivity相关久期；maturity单一期限不含支付分布。

questions.prompt: A Fixed Payment, a Changing Value: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: G price：amount exchanged now为价格；par面值不是任意现市成交额。

questions.prompt: A Fixed Payment, a Changing Value: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: H yield：payment stream与price计算收益率；coupon固定承诺利率不随当前成交价同变。

questions.prompt: A Fixed Payment, a Changing Value: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: E nominal：unadjusted inflation为名义；real实际正好是后空购买力调整。

questions.prompt: A Fixed Payment, a Changing Value: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: L real：purchasing-power adjusted为实际；nominal未调整不能替。

questions.prompt: A Fixed Payment, a Changing Value: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: C default：missed promised payment按例为违约；liquidity可卖性不同，premium溢价非不付款。

questions.explanation: B liquidity：ready sale without adverse price effect为流动性；default违约需付款未履约，与难卖可分开。

units.title: 六级选词：物品分类中的排他性与拥挤
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five words are not needed.

materials.title: Who Could Use the Same Resource?
materials.text:
An economics seminar classified goods by two properties rather than by the name of their owner. A good was ____1____ in the example when one person's use did not reduce the relevant benefit available to another. It was ____2____ when people could practically be prevented from using it under the stated arrangement.

A pure ____3____ good combined nonrival benefits with nonexclusion in the model. A ____4____ good combined rivalry with the practical ability to exclude. These categories described assumptions about use; they did not establish that every real object fitted one box under every technology.

A membership service with shared benefits and controlled entry was treated as a ____5____ good before capacity limits became important. A rival resource with difficult exclusion was a ____6____ resource in the seminar's terminology. The latter category did not itself specify a legal ownership regime or imply the absence of governance.

As use increased, ____7____ could reduce benefits through crowding. A facility that was effectively nonrival at low attendance might not remain so at every level of demand. Classification therefore required attention to capacity and the period considered.

The creation and organisation of a service concerned its ____8____. Paying for it concerned ____9____. A publicly funded service might be delivered by another organisation, so those roles could not be collapsed into the identity of one actor.

Finally, the rules of ____10____ determined who could actually enter and use the facility. A zero admission price alone did not show that every practical barrier had disappeared. Opening hours, location and capacity could still matter.

The framework helped students separate physical use, institutional arrangements and funding. It was an analytical starting point, not a shortcut from a label to the conclusion that one particular provider or payment system must be best.

questions.prompt: Who Could Use the Same Resource?: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: F nonrival：one use no reduced benefit为非竞争；free免费不保证不竞争。

questions.prompt: Who Could Use the Same Resource?: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: H excludable：practically prevent access为可排他；private私有法律身份并非能力定义。

questions.prompt: Who Could Use the Same Resource?: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: A public：nonrival+nonexclusion为纯公共品；collective一般集体不构成此经济分类特指。

questions.prompt: Who Could Use the Same Resource?: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: I private：rival+excludable为私人品；ownership法律归属不是两性质组合的分类名。

questions.prompt: Who Could Use the Same Resource?: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: D club：controlled entry shared benefits为俱乐部品；common难排他且竞争，下句不同。

questions.prompt: Who Could Use the Same Resource?: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: L common：rival difficult exclusion为公共池/共有资源；public纯公共品非竞争不同。

questions.prompt: Who Could Use the Same Resource?: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: J congestion：crowding lowers benefit为拥挤；scarcity泛稀缺不专指使用者增加造成的拥堵。

questions.prompt: Who Could Use the Same Resource?: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: N provision：creation organisation service为供给；financing只支付来源后空。

questions.prompt: Who Could Use the Same Resource?: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: E financing：paying for service为融资筹资；taxation税收仅一种筹资手段，文中泛指全部付款角色。

questions.prompt: Who Could Use the Same Resource?: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: B access：who enters/uses rules为准入；ownership所有权不直接等实际使用许可。

units.title: 六级选词：句法结构中的词序与依存
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five words are not needed.

materials.title: The Same Sequence, Two Structures
materials.text:
A syntax seminar compared analyses of written sentences. In one approach, a group of words functioning as a unit was a ____1____. Such a group could contain smaller groups, so sentence structure involved ____2____ rather than a flat list of equally related items.

Another approach highlighted a ____3____ between two words, a directed grammatical relation. One word served as the ____4____, organising the relation under the model's conventions. The seminar did not assume that every theoretical framework assigned all relations in the same way.

In a simple clause, the ____5____ was identified using stated grammatical tests rather than by automatically choosing the first word. A verb could show ____6____ with that element through matching features in the language under discussion. This relation was not merely two words having similar sounds.

A descriptive phrase could function as a ____7____, adding information to another expression. The choice of which expression it connected to was an ____8____ question. In a sentence describing someone observing a bird with binoculars, the written words alone could allow more than one such connection.

The resulting sentence was ____9____ because it supported distinct structural interpretations. Context might favour one reading, but that did not show that the written sequence encoded only that reading in isolation.

The seminar also examined ____10____, linking expressions such as two noun phrases with an appropriate conjunction. This differed from treating one phrase as a description inside another. The lesson used written examples and supplied all relevant relations; no missing tree diagram was required.

Students learned to separate word order from the organisation proposed to explain it. The same visible sequence could be compatible with alternative analyses, and theoretical terminology needed to be interpreted within the framework that defined it.
